basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: An authorized instruction to perform defined work, distinct from the work request that asked for it.
Holds scope, acceptance criteria and closure disposition, while task execution and time records live elsewhere.
Changes after authorization go through change control, unlike a free-form task list.
Closure records whether work was accepted, cancelled or deferred, not the asset state that resulted.

may: Draft a work order from an approved request with scope, location and acceptance criteria.
Report status and link completed work records.
Propose changes to scope or schedule as change requests.
Flag work orders past their due date or missing safety prerequisites.
mustNot: Release or authorize a work order without the authority to do so.
Expand scope or cost beyond the authorized limit without approved change.
Close a work order as complete when acceptance criteria were not met.
Skip permit-to-work, isolation or lockout requirements recorded for the job.
Delete a closed work order needed for maintenance history or audit.
requiresHuman: Authorizing work with safety, cost or contractual impact.
Accepting completed work against the criteria.
Cancelling a work order already in progress.

considerations: Hazardous work depends on the order carrying correct isolation and permit information; errors can injure workers.
Work order data is used to measure technicians and can be used unfairly without context.
Deferring safety-relevant work affects people who rely on the asset.
affectedParties: Technicians and contractors who perform the work
Occupants and users of the asset being worked on

items: A work order has an order number, an authorizer, a work location or asset, a scope statement and a status.
It is confused with a work request, a purchase order and a maintenance task procedure.
Injury when isolation or permit requirements are missing or ignored.
Work done on the wrong asset because of an ambiguous reference.
Duplicate orders causing repeated or conflicting work.
ISO 14224 for maintenance data in petroleum and natural gas industries.
IEC 62264 (ISA-95) for work and operations management.
MIMOSA OSA-EAI for asset management information exchange.
